subject: Data residency exception - DPIA runbook, evidence delivery and audit access
messages:
From: Lena Hofmann <lena.hofmann@hearthwell.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Reed <paul.reed@hearthwell.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPIA artefacts + residency exception for UK processing

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this on. As we discussed in the onboarding call, Hearthwell needs a short DPIA artefacts pack to support our internal board review for a UK-data residency exception. Specifically we need:

- A concise DPIA summary showing the lawful basis and risk mitigations for the planned processing.
- Article 28/30 register excerpts covering subprocessors involved in tokenization and logging.
- Evidence of KMS wrap/CMK usage for customer data at rest.
- A short runbook describing how Redwood will provide on-demand ledger extracts during an audit (format, lead times, sanitized fields).

Can you confirm:
1) Whether Redwood can provide a single downloadable archive for the above, or if pieces need to be shared via separate secure links?
2) What lead time you need to prepare the runbook and the ledger export (we'd like something by the end of next week if possible).

If helpful, Paul (cc'd) will coordinate legal/GRC questions. We expect this to be a lightweight intake, but the board wants everything in writing for the residency exception sign-off.

Thanks,
Lena

--
Lena Hofmann | Head of Security & Privacy

Subject: Re: DPIA artefacts + residency exception for UK processing

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. High-level plan:

- Marissa will own the DPIA summary + runbook draft.
- Ben will pull the Art.28/30 register excerpt and the ledger extract sample.
- Karthik (legal) will review wording for the residency exception and confirm any contract references we should include.

To your questions:
1) We can produce a single encrypted archive (preferred) and also provide individual secure links for any item you want to control separately.
2) Lead time: we can produce a draft runbook + sample ledger extract by EOD Friday, Oct 15 (8 business days). Finalized artifacts and the encrypted archive by Tuesday, Oct 19 assuming no heavy redlines from your team or legal.

Action items from our side:
- Marissa: first draft runbook (deliverable: dpia-runbook-v1.pdf).
- Ben: sample ledger extract (access-ledger-extract.csv) with column-level mapping and notes on redaction rules.
- Karthik: quick contract pointer to the DPA sections that cover audit access and subprocessor notification.

We'll share a Drive folder (link below) that will initially contain drafts and then the final artifacts in an encrypted ZIP with a separate password email.

Drive (private): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdeRunbook

I'll schedule a 30-min alignment call for Monday to walk through the runbook if you'd like.

Best,

Date: Fri, 8 Oct 2027 10:48:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: DPIA runbook & evidence checklist (dpia-runbook-v1.pdf attached)

Vanessa / team / Lena — attaching the first draft of the runbook and a short checklist. Highlights and assumptions up front:

- Scope: Inbound customer-provided text for model inference, transient KV caches, disk-encrypted artifacts, logs forwarded to the monitoring stack.
- Controls covered: KMS-wrapped storage, per-tenant encryption keys, prefix caching TTLs, automatic prefix redaction in exports.
- Audit access: We propose a two-tier delivery pattern: 1) immediate summary exports (within 48 hours) for operational review and 2) full ledger extracts for formal audits (5 business days, CSV with hash masking).

Key artifacts included in this update: dpia-runbook-v1.pdf (attached), access-ledger-extract.csv (sample attached).

Attachments:
- dpia-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook draft; includes export format spec and redaction rules)
- access-ledger-extract.csv (sample ledger, pseudonymized)

Open questions for Hearthwell:
- Are there specific fields you require redacted beyond the default mask we use (PII columns: user_email, user_id)?
- Do you prefer the encrypted archive via Drive or a secure SFTP endpoint?

If Lena/Paul confirm the redaction preferences I'll finalize the runbook and Ben will produce the Art.28/30 excerpt.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Privacy Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Lena Hofmann <lena.hofmann@hearthwell.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Paul Reed <paul.reed@hearthwell.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Oct 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: DPIA runbook & evidence checklist (dpia-runbook-v1.pdf attached)

Marissa — thank you, this is helpful. A few follow-ups from GRC: 

- Redaction: please also mask IP addresses and any free-text user_messages fields by default; we will not require user_email or user_id in ledger extracts.
- Delivery: encrypted Drive archive is fine for now; please send password in a separate email.
- KMS proof: can you include a small technical statement (one page) describing key wrap usage and a redacted key-ARN mapping, plus the kms-wrap-proof.pdf file? Our legal team wants a short write-up to reference in the board paper.
- Art28/30: we need an excerpt that shows dates for the most-recent subprocessor change (we had a recent swap for a logging provider). Please include a one-line change log entry and the legal clause pointer.

If you can include the above in the final archive, we'll be able to circulate to the board on Oct 20.

Best,
Lena
